translations.literal: The Hanshu chronological tables extend to all ministers and chief local officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Han the chronological tables cover every minister and prefectural chief.

translations.literal: The tables in the Ming History only go as far as the Seven Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming History tables stop at the Seven Ministers.

sentences.zh: 清增理藩院，蒙藏回諸部，都凡要務，於焉匯歸，輯民綏邊，所任殊重，與七卿等。

translations.literal: The Qing added the Board of Colonial Affairs for Mongol, Tibetan, and Muslim departments; all major affairs were gathered there; governing the people and securing the borders—the responsibilities were exceptionally weighty, equal to the Seven Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing added the Lifanyuan for the Mongol, Tibetan, and Muslim administrations; every major matter was routed there. Pacifying populations and stabilizing the frontiers made its charge as weighty as the Seven Ministers.

sentences.zh: 侍郎之屬，雖曰副貳，然與尚書皆爲敵體，題奏之草，有一不盡，例不得上，獎勩罰過，皆所與同。

translations.literal: Vice ministers, though called deputies, were equals of ministers; if any draft memorial was incomplete, by rule it could not be submitted; rewards, enfeoffments, penalties, and faults were all shared.
translations.idiomatic: Vice ministers were nominally deputies, yet they stood on equal footing with ministers: if a single memorial draft was incomplete, it could not by rule go up, and commendations, honors, penalties, and faults were all shared alike.

sentences.zh: 且內而樞輔，外而督撫，每由茲選，材雋所萃，未可闕也。

translations.literal: Moreover, inner Grand Councillors and outer governors-general and governors were often chosen from these ranks; talent gathered here and the posts could not be dispensed with.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillors within and governors-general and governors without were often selected from these offices; it was where outstanding talent concentrated and the ranks could not be spared.

sentences.zh: 光緒之季，增新汰舊，並於名稱亦多更易，依時爲表，期無舛漏。

translations.literal: In the late Guangxu era offices were added and old ones abolished, and many titles also changed; the tables follow the times so that nothing is missed or wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Guangxu reign new offices were created and old ones cut, and many titles were renamed besides; the tables are arranged by period so that no error or omission is left.

sentences.zh: 管部管院，權任亦重，以非官制，故概不書。

translations.literal: Superintendents of boards and courts also bore heavy authority, but because they were not regular institutions they are generally not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors of boards and yuans likewise held heavy power, but because they were not formal offices in the establishment they are generally not entered.
